text:
Maya: Heads-up — Peregrine-30B regional rollout planned for next Wed (EU then APAC). Expect change in token profile vs current models, need ops prep.
Liam: rough numbers from perf lab: Peregrine 30B single-shard steady-state ~11k t/s per GPU at 1.6k seq avg, burst to ~22k t/s with batching.
Dena: noted. What's the expected qps at ingress for a full EU rollout (no canary)?
Liam: if we route 100% traffic to Peregrine in EU we estimate ~3.6M t/s across the fleet (assuming 330 shards). That maps to ~3000 GPU-hours/day extra if autoscale keeps headroom at 20%.
Jonas: we should not do 100% flat roll — recommend staged canary: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 60% -> 100% across 48h windows.
Samir: cost eyeball? ballpark $/day for that 3k GPU-hours (using our reserved rate)?
Liam: ~ $48k/day at committed rates, ~ $72k/day at on-demand list — depends on reserved pool usage and quantized variant availability.
Dena: networking callout: cross-region peering + egress to APAC already at 78% on the ireland->singapore path. If APAC fans up we risk saturating egress during canary ramp.
NetBot: peering alert triggered last week at 82% for a short window; recommending we throttle non-essential background syncs during ramp (CDN bg syncs, telemetry exports).
Maya: ops plan: reserve additional 40 GPUs in eu-west pool as cold standby, pre-warm 12 GPUs with the quantized variant 6h before canary start. If canary telemetry looks clean, scale to warm 200 GPUs in 2h.
Jonas: autoscale tweaks — bump max-replicas by 25% for the eu-west autoscaler, lower scale-down aggression to avoid cache churn. Sample HPA patch:
```
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
spec:
  minReplicas: 10
  maxReplicas: 250
  metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: cpu
        target:
          type: Utilization
          averageUtilization: 60
```
Samir: can we fall back to a 7B variant automatically on overload? we should define a policy.
Maya: yes — routing policy will prefer Peregrine, but if latency > 750ms or gpu-queue > 80% for > 2m, route 25% to Peregrine-lite-7b automatically. Ops, please add that as a canary safety.
OpsBot: deploy pipeline created: `deploy/peregrine/regionized/v1` — canary percentages: 1,5,20,60. I will post status on each step.
Dena: request to Networking: please apply temporary egress cap to non-prod flows in eu-west during the 48h ramp window (window: Wed 02:00-50:00 UTC). Label: `peregrine-ramp-eu`.
NetBot: ack. Will apply rate-limits to telemetry and CI egress on Wed and raise peering capacity ticket with cloud provider if we hit 85%.
Jonas: health checks — enable KV-cache warm start and extend token-cache TTL to avoid cold starts during scale-up.
Maya: also track per-route cost delta and token/SLA regressions. Product: we'll run regen tests against 2k golden prompts at every step.
Samir: on-call ask: need 3 engineers in the 4h window after each major step (5%/20%/60%). I'll coordinate rota.
Maya: final ask — confirm reserved GPU top-up approved by finance for 72h buffer. If approved, we move pre-warm from cold->warm immediately.
Liam: added a small load test script we should run 2h before canary:
```
# quick local k6 job
k6 run --vus 300 --duration 15m load/peregrine-eu.js
```
Dena: one more: telemetry to look at — latency p95, gpu-queue, egress bytes, token/sec per-shard, and model-quality BLEU/ROUGE smoke tests.
Maya: thanks all. If no blockers I'll kick the plan Monday morning. @OpsBot please post updates during rollout. :rocket: :chart_with_upwards_trend:
